A four hundred dollar dinner with a client. CRA lets you deduct two hundred. Here's why.
Line eighty-five twenty-three: you claim fifty percent of the lesser of what you spent, or a reasonable amount.
Tips count as entertainment, so they fall under the same limit.
Our Manitoba consultant is self-employed and earns sixty thousand. Twelve client dinners a year, four hundred each.
That's forty-eight hundred spent. Only twenty-four hundred comes off income.
Tax and CPP saved: about eight hundred fifty-four dollars. Roughly seventy-one per dinner.
So those dinners still cost about thirty-nine fifty.
One exception: bill the meal to your client and show it on the invoice, and the fifty percent limit doesn't apply.
